resources.string: Out until you pick up the phone
Shh. The first unlock in the morning wakes him.
The screen was on too long. See what he found.
He\'ll come back when you pick up the phone.
A quick look is fine. If the screen stays on too long, he\'ll turn back.
Asleep since %1$s. The first unlock after five in the morning wakes him.
Brr. Good thing I have my scarf. Plug me in?
He sleeps best by a burning stove: put the phone on charge first.
Start with a short outing: send him out and put the phone face down for a quarter of an hour.
Everything is there: off to the workshop!
The pantry is empty. Send me out, I\'ll find something.
Two or three things together make a proper meal in the kitchen.
He grows into the way you live together.
Slept %1$s h, the screen was on %2$d min
He brought something back from his dream:
%1$s is out. Plan the next outing when he\'s back.
Until I pick up the phone
He walks while the phone lies still. Pick it up and he comes home.
Finds if he goes all the way: about %1$d
Put the phone face down and get on with something else. A quick look is fine, but if the screen stays on he\'ll turn back.
He\'s waiting at the hatch with a bundle. Off to: %1$s.
This phone can\'t tell when it lies face down. Tap the button and put it away.
Make things from finds: tools open new districts, furniture goes into the nook, clothes he wears.
Cook from the pantry: a dish fills him up more than its bits would on their own.
Tilt the phone to roll him to the sugar.
Drag across the maze to roll him to the sugar.
Sugar! I\'ll take it to the pantry.
Made it! That\'s enough sugar for today, I\'m just playing now.
Hi. I live in your phone.
Between the boards, next to the battery. When you charge the phone it\'s warm in here, and when it runs down it\'s cold. I feel it when you shake the phone, and I see it when the lights go out.
What\'s my name? And what colour am I?
Or show me a photo: your cat, a favourite jumper, the sea. I\'ll take its colour.
One thing about me: I\'m happiest when you put the phone down.
Turn the phone face down and I\'ll go out into the districts inside it. The longer it lies there, the further I go and the more I find.
In the evening put me to bed by the stove: put the phone on charge. If the screen stays dark till morning, I sleep well and bring something back from my dreams.
From what I find we\'ll make tools to reach new districts, furniture and clothes, and cook proper food.

A nook inside your phone. The stove is the battery: it burns while the phone charges and goes cold when it runs down. Tap me to stroke me. Below you can see if I\'m fed and how I feel; the tiles are what we can do together.

From here I go out into the phone. Pick a place and how long, then turn the phone face down. While it lies there I walk and pick things up. A quick peek is fine; a long scroll and I come back halfway. New places open with tools from the workshop.
Everything I\'ve found lives here. Dark shapes are things still waiting somewhere in the phone. Tap a find to see where it turns up and what it\'s good for. Crumbs and raisins are food.
We make things from finds. Tools open new places, furniture goes into the nook, I wear the clothes. What counts is the shape: any thread will do as thread. In the kitchen we cook proper meals.
Tilt the phone and I\'ll roll along the tracks. Get me to the sugar: the first two lumps a day go to the pantry.
Rustle in his nook: how he is, and buttons to feed him and send him out
Open the app to move him in
Out: %1$s, until you pick up the phone
The pantry is empty: send him out first
Off he goes: %1$s. Put the phone down
Who am I? Pick the one that looks like me.
A day counts if you fed him, stroked him, sent him out, put him to bed or played.
For each one he gives back a present, mostly something not yet in your collection. New requests every Monday.
He\'s cheerful: outings of 25 minutes or more bring one find more.
Outings bring the usual haul. Cheer him up for a bonus.
He\'s glum or hungry: outings bring less. Feed him, stroke him.
Goes up: strokes (a dozen a day count), outings all the way, good nights, cooked meals, the maze, his requests, the morning greeting.
Goes down: slowly by itself, and after a restless night.
4–5 hearts: one find more from outings of 25 minutes or longer. 0–1 heart: one find fewer.
Goes down by itself all day long. Feed him from the pantry; dishes from the kitchen fill him up more than plain food.
0–1 crumb: he is hungry and brings one find fewer.
Do them before Sunday is out: each one done, he gives you something in return.
Collect them on outings; when the pantry has enough, tap “Hand it over”.
Counts outings since Monday that went all the way.
Put him to bed on charge in the evening; a good night is one with the screen dark till morning.
Kinds of finds you didn\'t have before, found since Monday.
The nook itself keeps its colours: it lights itself.
if the phone puts the app to sleep
report a bug, suggest an idea, chat
The camera window can show the real sky where you are: sunrise and sunset, clouds, rain, snow, fog and storms.
The phone doesn\'t know where it is yet. Turn on location for a moment and try again.
Only an approximate location is used, rounded to about a kilometre, and it goes only to the weather service (Open-Meteo, or MET Norway as a fallback).
Let me look out on your town: real sunsets, rain and snow. An approximate location is enough.
Put him on the home screen: his corner of the nook, how he is, and buttons to feed him, stroke him and send him out.
On each screen he explains what\'s what the first time you open it.
If outings stop on their own

Some phones (Xiaomi, Huawei, Samsung) put apps to sleep in the background. If he comes home empty-handed or a night doesn\'t count, let Rustle run in the background: no battery restrictions, autostart on.
Rustle is one of the StillCraft apps. Tell us what\'s broken or what\'s missing.
a message when a new version is out
for stove wood and new outings
Rustle %1$s. Everything stays on the phone. The internet is used only for the weather in the window, if you turn it on. Font: m6x11 by Daniel Linssen.
A week has gone by and the glass is dusty. There is a cloth ready (%1$d in the drawer).
A week has gone by and the glass is dusty. He needs a cloth: sew one in the workshop from three threads.
%1$s is rubbing the glass from the inside. The dust is flying!
The cloth is worn through, but the glass shines. %1$s is very pleased.
The phone has caught Wi-Fi. %1$s can pop into the Net for %2$d minutes and tell you what is going on out there. Once a day.
He is only looking around. No need to put the phone down.
%1$s will be back in %2$d minutes with news.
%1$s is in the Net. Plan an outing when he is back.
News of the world, as he tells it
That will do for now: three is plenty.
